snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Victory Hook: Simulation 1. Unit 8 heavy. 45 mins. Attempt all. Recall the roots.

quick_notes.title: Unit 8 Weightage
quick_notes.detail: High. Focus on Sangam literature, Chola administration, and Palayakarar revolts.
quick_notes.explanation: Unit 8 is important because it carries a high weightage, meaning many questions come from this unit. Sangam literature refers to the oldest body of Tamil poems, composed between 300 BCE and 300 CE by poets gathered in academies called Sangams. Chola administration means the system of government used by the Chola dynasty, which included organized village assemblies, a strong bureaucracy, and land revenue systems. Palayakarar revolts were armed uprisings led by local chieftains called Palayakarars (also known as Poligars) in the late 18th century, who fought against the British East India Company's control. Focus your study on these three topics: Sangam literature, Chola administration, and the Palayakarar revolts.

quick_notes.title: Time Management
quick_notes.detail: 45 mins for 100 questions. No negative marking in TNPSC, so attempt ALL.
quick_notes.explanation: In the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC) exam, you have 45 minutes to answer 100 questions. This means you have less than 30 seconds per question, so you must work quickly. There is no negative marking, which means you will not lose any marks for giving a wrong answer. Because of this, you should answer every single question, even if you have to guess, because an unanswered question gives you zero marks while a guessed answer might be correct.

quick_notes.title: Elimination
quick_notes.detail: Use the logic of landscapes (Thinai) to solve literature questions.
quick_notes.explanation: In the Tamil literary tradition, a Thinai is a specific type of landscape or region, such as a mountain, forest, or seashore, that is used to set the mood and theme of a poem. Each Thinai is linked to a particular time of day, season, and a set of emotions or activities, like love or war. To solve a literature question using the logic of Thinai, you first identify the landscape described in the poem, for example, a desert or a field. Then, you match that landscape to its traditional Thinai name, such as Palai for a dry, barren land. Once you know the Thinai, you can eliminate wrong answer choices that describe a different landscape, time, or emotion, because each Thinai has its own fixed rules. This method helps you find the correct answer by focusing only on the details that fit the specific Thinai of the poem.
